title: Gilead Deepens Oncology Reach And HIV Prevention With Arcellx And Lenacapavir

Gilead Sciences (NasdaqGS:GILD) has completed all regulatory approvals for its acquisition of Arcellx, finalizing the year's largest biopharmaceutical deal. The company is also widening access to its long acting HIV prevention therapy lenacapavir through expanded international programs and partnerships.

For readers watching large cap biopharma, these two developments show where Gilead is currently focusing its efforts: cell therapy and HIV prevention. Arcellx adds to Gilead's cell therapy and oncology capabilities, an area where many large drug companies are investing heavily. Lenacapavir sits at the center of long acting HIV prevention, a segment that is drawing attention from both public health agencies and private payers.

Looking ahead, investors may want to track how Gilead integrates Arcellx's research pipeline and technology platforms into its existing oncology franchise. It can also be useful to follow how quickly international access initiatives for lenacapavir move from announcements into on the ground availability, since that can influence uptake patterns, partnerships, and future capital allocation decisions at Gilead.

The Arcellx acquisition and expanded lenacapavir access point in the same direction for Gilead, toward a deeper presence in oncology and HIV prevention that sits alongside its existing virology base. Arcellx gives Gilead additional cell therapy assets and technology that can sit next to Kite’s Yescarta franchise and potentially sharpen its position versus large oncology peers such as Bristol Myers Squibb and Novartis. On the HIV side, committing to reach about 3 million people with lenacapavir by 2028 through international partners links directly to long term access, policy, and reimbursement themes that many investors are already watching in this company.

How This Fits Into The Gilead Sciences Narrative

The Arcellx deal and lenacapavir access push align with the narrative catalyst around expanding oncology, cell therapy, and next generation HIV regimens as key growth drivers. Higher spending needs for large transactions such as the US$7.8b Arcellx buyout and the separate Tubulis agreement could test the narrative’s assumption of disciplined expense management and margin improvement if integration or R&D costs run high. The specific scale of lenacapavir access commitments and the size of the Arcellx deal are not fully reflected in the narrative’s qualitative focus on access and oncology, so investors may want to factor these into their own long term scenarios.

From here, the key items to track are how quickly the Arcellx transaction closes and how Gilead outlines timelines, indications, and cost expectations for the combined cell therapy portfolio. title: Gilead Receives All Required Regulatory Approvals for the Acquisition of Arcellx and Extends Tender Offer
content:
FOSTER CITY, Calif., April 17, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) announced today that all required regulatory approvals have been obtained for its previously announced acquisition of Arcellx and that Gilead has extended the expiration of the tender offer to purchase all outstanding shares of common stock of Arcellx.

On April 13, 2026, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) published its decision that the acquisition of Arcellx may be put into effect, subject to expiration of a 14-calendar day waiting period. Assuming that the ACCC’s determination remains unchallenged during this waiting period, the waiting period expires at 10:00 a.m., Eastern Time, on April 27, 2026. Additionally, the relevant review period for the Austrian competition authorities has expired. Accordingly, all required regulatory approvals for the transaction have been obtained, and the "Regulatory Approvals Condition" (as defined in the Offer to Purchase, dated March 6, 2026, relating to the offer) will be satisfied upon expiration of the 14-calendar day review period pursuant to Australian competition law.

The tender offer, which was previously scheduled to expire at 5:00 p.m., Eastern Time, on April 24, 2026, has been extended to expire at 5:00 p.m., Eastern Time, on April 27, 2026, and remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions, including the tender of a number of shares of Arcellx common stock that, together with shares already owned by Gilead, equals at least a majority of the then-outstanding Arcellx shares and other customary offer conditions.

The offer remains at a purchase price of (1) $115.00 per share, net to the seller in cash, without interest, subject to any withholding tax, plus (2) one contractual contingent value right (CVR), which represents the right to receive one contingent payment of $5.00 per CVR in cash, without interest, and subject to any withholding tax, payable on March 31, 2030, subject to cumulative worldwide sales of Arcellx’s anitocabtagene autoleucel (anito-cel) product exceeding $6.0 billion on or prior to December 31, 2029.

Computershare Trust Company, N.A., the depositary and paying agent for the tender offer, has advised Gilead that, as of 4:00 p.m., Eastern Time, on April 16, 2026, approximately 10,271,823 shares have been validly tendered and not validly withdrawn in the tender offer, representing approximately 17.5% of the outstanding shares as of such date and time. Holders that have previously tendered their shares do not need to re-tender their shares or take any other action in response to the extension of the tender offer. Questions or requests for assistance may be directed to Innisfree M&A Incorporated, the information agent for the tender offer, by calling toll free (877) 800-5182.

Story Continues

About Gilead Sciences

Gilead Sciences, Inc. is a biopharmaceutical company that has pursued and achieved breakthroughs in medicine for more than three decades, with the goal of creating a healthier world for all people. The company is committed to advancing innovative medicines to prevent and treat life-threatening diseases, including HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19, and cancer. In 2025, Gilead announced a planned $32 billion investment to further strengthen its U.S. footprint to power the next era of discovery, job creation and public health preparedness – while continuing to invest globally to ensure patients everywhere benefit from its scientific innovation. Gilead operates in more than 35 countries worldwide, with headquarters in Foster City, Calif.

title: Gilead’s Tubulis Deal Recasts Oncology Ambitions And HIV Reliance Risks
content:
Get insights on thousands of stocks from the global community of over 7 million individual investors at Simply Wall St.

Gilead Sciences is acquiring Tubulis GmbH in a deal worth up to $5b, its third major transaction in six weeks. The Tubulis deal brings next generation antibody drug conjugate technology and a pipeline of cancer therapies into Gilead’s oncology portfolio. Gilead has also acquired Arcellx and Ouro Medicines and exercised licensing options with Kymera Therapeutics and Cartography Biosciences to expand its cancer and autoimmune pipeline.

For investors tracking NasdaqGS:GILD, these moves come as the company leans further into oncology while its HIV franchise faces growing competitive and policy pressures. The share price sits at $139.03, with a 1 year return of 37.7% and a 5 year return of 150.5%. This indicates that the stock has already seen substantial interest over a multi year period.

The Tubulis acquisition, together with recent deals and licensing arrangements, indicates a clear intention to build a broader cancer and autoimmune portfolio. Readers may want to watch how Gilead executes on integrating these assets, advancing its antibody drug conjugate platform and managing the shift in revenue mix away from legacy products over time.

📰 Beyond the headline: 1 risk and 4 things going right for Gilead Sciences that every investor should see.

For Gilead, the Tubulis acquisition and a string of recent deals with Arcellx, Ouro Medicines, Kymera and Cartography look less like one off events and more like a reset of how the company wants to compete in cancer. Tubulis brings antibody drug conjugate technology that aims to deliver chemotherapy directly to tumors, while Kymera’s KT 200 degrader and Cartography’s tumor selective targets broaden the types of oncology drugs Gilead can work on. The expanded Tempus AI collaboration adds data and analytics to help choose the right patients and indications for these assets. Together, this shifts more of Gilead’s R&D engine into oncology and autoimmune conditions as its HIV portfolio faces political and pricing scrutiny, including criticism over HIV drug costs in Florida. Investors watching large peers such as Roche, Pfizer and Merck may see Gilead using M&A and partnerships to stay relevant in areas like antibody drug conjugates and cell therapy where many big pharma groups are spending heavily.

How This Fits Into The Gilead Sciences Narrative

The push into oncology and immune disorders through Tubulis, Arcellx and Ouro lines up with the narrative that Gilead is trying to reduce dependence on legacy HIV products and build a broader, higher value portfolio. Heavy deal making and licensing introduces execution and integration questions that challenge the cleaner margin and earnings path set out in the narrative, especially if timelines slip or assets underperform expectations. The expanded Tempus AI collaboration and the specific ADC and degrader platforms from Tubulis and Kymera are not fully captured in the high level narrative, which focuses more on end markets than on how data and drug modality choices might influence long term product mix.

Any early clinical data, safety updates or partnership milestones will help clarify whether these oncology acquisitions are building a coherent franchise or adding complexity without clear payback. It is also worth keeping an eye on how management talks about HIV pricing pressure and any changes to capital allocation, given the roughly US$20b of oncology related deals in a short period.

With Arcellx trading around US$114.80, a recent intrinsic value estimate points to a large discount. However, the stock also sits slightly above one analyst price target. Is this a genuine opportunity, or is the market already pricing in future growth?

Price to Book of 16.7x: Is it justified?

Arcellx is currently trading on a P/B of 16.7x, and that sits well below a peer group average of 42.1x but far above the wider US biotech industry average of 2.2x.

The P/B ratio compares the market value of the company to its book value, so for a clinical stage biotech with limited revenue and ongoing losses it often reflects how investors are weighing the pipeline and intellectual property rather than current earnings power.
